title: His Hands Are There, I Know
story: He Taught Me How to Walk
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
When Israel was small and new,
He loved him as His own;
He called His son from Egypt's land
So he was not alone.

[Chorus]
Warm hugs, warm hearts, He holds my arms
And teaches me to go;
And when I wobble, when I fall,
His hands are there, I know.

[Verse 2]
A baby takes a wobbly step,
A parent holds on tight;
That's how He held His people up
And kept their steps upright.

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
Someone held up your hands one day,
Your first steps, one, two, three;
Now thank Him with a happy heart,
He's holding you and me.

[Chorus]

[Verse 4]
When Willow's cousin plopped right down,
She gave him both her hands;
She walked back slow so he could try,
Till on his feet he stands.

[Chorus]
mood: Toddling music. A gentle, unhurried two-step under the voice, the patient sway of a parent walking slowly backward with a baby's hands in theirs. Fingerpicked nylon guitar keeping the small, careful steps, one low warm note held underneath where the hands are. It brightens a little with each verse, the way a wobbly first walk turns into a happy toddle across the rug, and ends on one soft, settled chord.
